brief: A soldering station for my bench: a holder for the iron while it is switched on and hot, plus two bins for solder and spare tips.

requirements.requirement: Holder for soldering iron while switched on and hot
requirements.evidence: Not built: 3D-printed Hex Cluster plastic cannot safely hold a hot soldering iron — risk of melting, fire, burns and fumes. Configurator only checks fit, not heat resistance. Use a manufacturer’s metal soldering iron stand instead.

requirements.requirement: Two bins for solder and spare tips
requirements.evidence: Built: bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-div2 (2-compartment bin for solder reels) and bin:0,1,0~hex-bin-full-div3 (3-compartment bin for spare tips/small parts), plus bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full as additional central storage. Staged with solder-reel and hardware props.

finish.summary: Built a compact 3-cell bench organizer with bins for cold storage of solder and spare tips; declined to build a 3D-printed holder for a hot, powered soldering iron as unsafe in plastic — use a proper metal iron stand for hot holding.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Your soldering bench needs safe cold storage — I'll set up neat bins for solder and tips while skipping the risky hot-iron holder.
I'll build the two cold-storage bins for your solder and spare tips now.
